result.title: Weight-Space Programming Doesn't Need Transformers
result.summary: Standard neural architectures such as the Transformer were chosen because they train well with gradient descent and run fast on GPUs. In weight-space programming, a large language model (LLM) writes target weights by hand without gradient-based training, so those reasons no longer apply. Should we keep the Transformer? Given minimal guidance, ten labeled examples, and a sandbox, mainly on multiple-choice questions, we task three frontier LLMs with either generating the weights of a fixed architecture or designing the architecture themselves. When free to design, all three compile plain-text facts into a sparse table queried by a fixed procedure, reaching up to 54.4% test accuracy. An LLM-designed model achieves higher test accuracy than the most accurate released Transformer that the same LLM wrote while using about 1,800x fewer parameters. Without gradients, they choose a table, in which the LLM can state what each weight means and can find and rewrite a wrong one. Each wrong answer points to one row, and removing a row changes about one other answer. From this, we propose an associative-memory-based model up to 17x faster on GPUs than a same-sized Transformer. We also test pretrained weights, other benchmarks, and tasks where models generate answers. Pretrained LLMs remain more accurate; the claim concerns which structure to build when writing weights.

AI.brief_summary: 论文考察「weight-space programming」：在无梯度训练、仅给定少量标注样例和沙盒的条件下，让三个前沿 LLM 直接写出固定架构的权重或自行设计架构，发现自由设计时它们都收敛到稀疏查表加固定查询流程，以约 1/1800 的参数量超过同一 LLM 手写的 Transformer，并据此提出联想记忆式模型。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本多选题、无视觉与推理轨迹，与 LVR 主线联系弱；但「稀疏表 + 固定查表过程」这种可读出权重含义、删去一行只改变约一个答案的显式状态结构，可能为 latent 状态的可解释性、贡献分配与计算成本比较提供参照，可供核查。
